newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia PM blasts speculations, seeks cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia PM blasts speculations, seeks cooperation.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad on Thursday lashed out at "rogue speculators" whom he says are undermining Southeast Asian economies, and urged more cooperation amongst countries to combat such forces.

Opening the 30th foreign ministerial meetings of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN), Mahathir said: "We see a well-planned effort to undermine the economies of all the ASEAN countries by destabilising their currencies.
"Our economic fundamentals are good, yet anyone with a few billion dollars can destroy all the progress that we have made," he said.

Asked if he was satisfied with the coordination of central banks in the region to defend their currencies, Mahathir told reporters after the speech, "Actually it could be improved...everything can be improved."
In the past few years, central banks of the region and the Bank of Japan have struck repurchase pacts under which they would help each other defend their currencies if asked.

Mahathir did not spell out how the monetary authorities might boost their cooperation. "We already have some cooperation and arrangements. Obviously it is not sufficient or effective enough to deal with the kind of situation we are facing now," he said.
Malaysia and neighbouring countries have seen attacks on their currencies in the past month, forcing devaluations in Thailand and the Philippines and expensive intervention efforts in Malaysia.
On Thursday, regional currencies dropped to new lows as speculators and corporates continued to pile into the dollar, triggering stop-loss orders.

Earlier on Thursday, the Thai baht dropped to a low of 32.63/dollar onshore, the Singapore dollar fell below the psychological level of 1.4700 on stop-loss sales while the Malaysian ringgit breached the 2.65 barrier in early trade on spillover weakness from Thailand and Singapore.
The Indonesian rupiah slipped back through the 2,600 support level on Thursday.
Mahathir, known for his sharp-tongued criticisms of the West, said the countries of the region were told they must open up their markets and that trade and commerce must be totally free.

"Free for whom? For rogue speculators. For anarchists wanting to destroy weak countries in their crusade for open societies, to force us to submit to the dictatorship of international manipulators," Mahathir told the ASEAN gathering.
"We want to embrace borderlessness but we still need to protect ourselves from self serving rogues and international brigandage," he said.
Asked later by reporters which speculators he meant, Mahathir said he did not want to name names.
Mahathir said he believed fundamentals in the region were still sound.

"Most companies in ASEAN countries are doing well in comparison to Europe," he said in answer to questions. "To give that (poor fundamentals) as an excuse for attacking currencies and trying to profiteer from this situation is not good enough."

Malaysia is the current chairman of ASEAN, which was expanded on Wednesday to nine members with the inclusion of Laos and Burma. Its other members are Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, Indonesia, Brunei and Singapore.
Cambodia had been due to be admitted at the same time as Laos and Burma but ASEAN ministers delayed its entry to Phnom Penh's current political crisis.
